item.title: Woman covertly filmed by Meta smart glasses raises privacy concerns
item.description: One woman is speaking out after she was secretly filmed, saying that technology like Meta's AI-powered smart glasses threatens personal privacy.

item.title: Drug mix-up at Nashville hospital causes dire complications in 4 patients
item.description: Four patients at Ascension Saint Thomas Midtown received incorrect medications last week, CBS affiliate WTVF reported.

item.title: AI companies accused of hoarding and destroying millions of books
item.description: Consumer advocates are urging the FTC to examine whether AI developers are hurting competition and reducing public access to source material.

item.title: Why Lindsay Clancy didn't testify in her murder trial
item.description: The defense rested Friday in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial without Clancy taking the stand. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down why.

item.title: Watch Live: Lindsay Clancy trial defense rests, prosecution calls new witnesses
item.description: The defense rested in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial Friday in Massachusetts. The prosecution has started calling rebuttal witnesses.

item.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows work on White House ballroom to continue
item.description: Chief Justice John Roberts issued a stay that will remain in place until the Supreme Court takes further action.

item.title: Supreme Court temporarily allows Trump's White House ballroom construction to continue
item.description: The Supreme Court has issued a temporary stay in the case over President Trump's White House ballroom, allowing construction to continue as the legal challenge plays out. CBS News chief legal correspondent Jan Crawford has more.

item.title: Iran touts its trade ties as U.S. turns from bombs to economic warfare
item.description: As Vice President JD Vance declares economic pressure "the most effective tool that we have," Iran seeks to show deepening trade ties with its neighbors.

item.title: Cardiac event reveals Olympian's rare heart condition: "There was a God present"
item.description: Olympian Jenny Simpson said she won't be able to run again after being diagnosed with a rare heart condition earlier this year.

item.title: Court says prosecutor who subpoenaed Letitia James was unlawfully appointed
item.description: A federal appeals court said the top federal prosecutor in the Northern District of New York was unlawfully serving when he subpoenaed state Attorney General Letitia James.

item.title: Pentagon moves to fire publisher and editor of Stars and Stripes
item.description: The Pentagon has given separation notices to both the publisher and the editor-in-chief of Stars and Stripes, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Psychiatrist in Andrea Yates case testifies for Lindsay Clancy's defense
item.description: The defense rested Friday in Lindsay Clancy's murder trial after testimony from Dr. Phillip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist who also testified Andrea Yates case after she killed her five children in Texas in 2001. Clancy has admitted to killing her three young children, but has pleaded not guilty, arguing she was overmedicated and suffering from postpartum psychosis. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has more.

item.title: National Weather Service confirms tornado struck N.Y.'s Atlantic Beach
item.description: The National Weather Service confirmed a tornado struck Long Island's Atlantic Beach Thursday evening. It's the first confirmed tornado in Nassau County since 2021.

item.title: 8 dead in charter plane crash near remote military radar site in Alaska
item.description: The crash of a small plane in Alaska chartered by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers is under investigation.

item.title: Is Michael Cohen pushing for a pardon in reunion with Trump?
item.description: President Trump and his former fixer Michael Cohen held a radio reunion Thursday, seemingly ending a years-long feud that stemmed from Cohen's testimony against the president both in court and before Congress. CBS News' Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Human remains found in Lake Powell amid shrinking water levels
item.description: Another set of human remains was found in Lake Mead earlier this week. Both reservoirs are dealing with low water levels.

item.title: Defense rests case in Lindsay Clancy trial
item.description: The defense for Lindsay Clancy has rested their case in the murder trial over the killings of Clancy's three young children. CBS News legal contributor Rebecca Roiphe has more.

item.title: Meta AI glasses spark fears about privacy
item.description: Meta's glasses that are capable of recording video may pose a threat to people's privacy, critics say.

item.title: Grief coach describes sending her daughter "out on a rocket ship of love" when she died
item.description: Author and grief coach Kate Doerge told Norah O'Donnell that when her family was told that her daughter Penny, who was battling neurofibromatosis, had an inoperable tumor, she opened the doors to her house for people to come and celebrate the 16-year-old. "We sent her out on a rocket ship of love," Doerge said on "Healthful."

item.title: NASA scraps mission to save Swift telescope that will plunge toward Earth
item.description: NASA is pivoting from a mission to save the Swift telescope. CBS News' Bill Harwood explains why.

item.title: IndyCar is holding its first race in D.C. this weekend. Here's what to know.
item.description: Twenty-five cars traveling at top speeds approaching 180 mph will zoom around the National Mall this weekend when IndyCar takes over downtown D.C.

item.title: AI could be used to generate bills that may become laws. Here are the concerns.
item.description: The use of artificial intelligence on Capitol Hill could pose some issues for bills that may become U.S. laws later on. Ari Hershowitz, founder of DreamProIT, joins CBS News with his take.

item.title: Trump to honor Artemis II crew with nation's top space medal
item.description: President Trump plans to award the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the crew​ of NASA's Artemis II mission​ in a ceremony Aug. 28.

item.title: Nearly 25% of workers are "functionally unemployed," analysis finds
item.description: An alternative measure of unemployment that accounts for wages suggests the U.S. labor market is weaker than it looks.

item.title: Trump temporarily waives higher beef tariffs in bid to lower prices
item.description: Ground beef prices, now averaging nearly $7 a pound, remain historically high due to shrinking cattle herds.

item.title: Surrogate who had baby against parents' wishes unlikely to win custody battle, attorney says
item.description: A surrogate rejected a request from the biological parents to end her pregnancy after they discovered the baby had a severe heart condition. Baby Rumi underwent the first of three surgeries after being born. Now, the surrogate says the biological parents are suing her. Alexis Cirel, an attorney specializing in family and fertility law, weighs in on the custody lawsuit.

item.title: Trump appears on radio show of Michael Cohen, patching up public split
item.description: President Trump appeared on the radio show of Michael Cohen, his fixer-turned-foe, in a stunning public reunion that would have been impossible to imagine several years ago.

item.title: This violinist's music comforted people in NYC after 9/11 — when she was just 11
item.description: Magee Capsouto played her violin in her parents' restaurant near Ground Zero in the days after Sept. 11, 2001.

item.title: NYC changed forever on 9/11. A look back at what unfolded.
item.description: NYC and the nation are vowing to "never forget" what happened during the 9/11 attack 24 years ago today.

item.title: Firefighter keeps memory of 9/11 alive for those too young to remember
item.description: The last firefighter to escape the North Tower shares his story with teachers and students to make sure the memory of 9/11 is never lost to future generations.
